question: Within matched cages where both shapes are geometrically possible, can the rest of the vacancy mask discriminate the realized tripod from the opposite-pair T, beyond counting feasible orientations? This conditions on the event; it is not a forecast of its occurrence. The species-summed Gibbs law sees the entire exterior vacancy mask including the near halo, not only a distant shell. Colored halo and mask are different conditioning sets. This does not reverse the distant-shell negative, establish equilibration, or measure repeated cavities, dynamics or recurrence.
cohorts: Reuse the known near-halo positive-control cohorts and release/receipt pins in near-design.json, explicitly NOT a new holdout. Sole primary: all 2048 native index-7 validation parents. Descriptive: first 1024 index-9 validation parents in native split order (never extract physical rows from the reserved half); then all 2048 index-0 native validation parents. Retain all roster rows, including zero denominators. No other temperatures, training, testing, new configurations, physical sampling or repeated scoring.
screen: Scan each periodic native z,y,x origin: observe whether center vacant, exactly 3 occupied arms, sorted coordination of those occupied arms 3,3,5. Record realized shape only for outcomes and checks. Enumerate all 20 sets of 3 occupied arms in the same native coordinate frame: admissible if their coordination in the supplied exterior has the fixed signature. Tripod = one arm per axis; T = one complete opposite pair. The partition is unchanged under complementation. Ambiguity requires positive counts of BOTH shapes using only this exterior enumeration; identical screen, sample and weights for all models, regardless of the observed orbit. Forced cases enter census only, never the primary score.
selection: Sort ambiguous matched centers by native flat origin. Retain all up to 4 per parent; otherwise take 4 uniformly without replacement using PCG64([772191, beta_index, native_row]). Never condition the draw on shape, species or forecast. Each selected center represents n_amb/min(n_amb,4) centers; use exact full ambiguous counts in denominators and Horvitz-Thompson numerator totals. The target is the full ambiguous-center population weighted by centers, not one average per parent. Also report actual full-census prevalences, ambiguous parents, scored parents and actual number scored.
predictor: No species or core occupancy input. On the periodic lattice retain only mask bits at taxicab distance at least 2 from center. Directly census occupied sites beyond distance 2 using only their six exterior neighbors. These unaffected coordination bins are invariant to any core/arm filling: their closed neighborhoods are disjoint from the hidden cross. Assert this lookup disjointness for every relative site; independently compare the direct census to the observed-parent outside census for the first scored center in each cohort, never using it for the forecast. For each admissible arm mask B add two occupied k=3 arms and one k=5 arm, then add every occupied distance-2 site's count k=m0_j+s_j(B), where m0_j counts occupied distance-3 neighbors and s_j counts incident occupied candidate arms. All seven bins must be nonnegative and total 6000 for every mask.
law: For each resulting census evaluate ln Z_species at the known beta, summing ALL A/B assignments at fixed N_A=2400, with energies (k-3)^2 and (k-5)^2. Include the reference-energy term, not just assignment odds or a fitted chemical potential. Group feasible orientations by shape and normalize exp(ln Z), with a shared max shift. Compute observed log scores in log space. Uniform baseline gives equal mass per feasible orientation (not per shape). At beta zero verify identical ln Z across orientations and exact equality to the uniform probability and score. The existing colored near_cage_law exact halo probability (only L1=2,3 exterior species) is a distinct privileged-information comparator; it supplies neither the eligibility screen nor any vacancy-predictor features. Use its existing ambivalent-support endpoint correction only for its logs, and count repairs.
decision: Pass only if lower endpoint of the two-sided parent-clustered 95% interval for realized vacancy-marginal minus uniform-feasible paired log score at index 7 is >=0.01 nat per ambiguous matched center. No selection among metrics, fitting, temperature pooling or retries. Missing interval is inconclusive. Other cohorts and comparisons are descriptive.
inference: Ratio of sums over native parents, including zeros. Pair scores before inference. SE=sqrt(P/(P-1) sum_i (d_i-G*w_i)^2)/sum_i w_i, G=sum_i d_i/sum_i w_i; t_(P-1,.975) interval. Exact census denominator w_i=n_amb for ambiguous forecasts, n_matched for forced fraction or all-match prevalence. Rows with no centers have zero numerator and denominator. Zero total denominator gives null estimate, fewer than two contributing parents no interval. Calibration residual is the paired inverse-inclusion weighted sum of (observed tripod minus forecast), divided by full ambiguous count. Report ambiguous prevalence, forced fraction, observed log scores, tripodal probabilities, observed minus predicted, colored minus vacancy and each model minus feasible, plus realized classification accuracy (tie predicts tripod).
artifacts: Exclusive vacancy-run.json before archive access; vacancy-parents-II.npz stores parent/lineage, census counts, number drawn and weighted sufficient sums. vacancy-score-II.json and vacancy-results.json bind artifacts with SHA256 and identify cohort, score units, decision and limitations. Single new figure vacancy-ambiguous.png plots within-ambiguous contrasts and calibration. No existing score or image is overwritten.
